summary: In civil spaceflight, NASA astronauts conducted a 6.5-hour spacewalk to prepare the International Space Station for solar array upgrades, as NASA and Roscosmos agreed to continue their joint crew seat barter arrangement. In commercial launch developments, Rocket Lab successfully placed a Japanese Earth-observing satellite into orbit following a five-week delay, secured a $397 million contract to build threat-tracking satellites, and Blue Origin identified a faulty oxygen valve as the cause of a recent New Glenn rocket explosion. Additionally, Chinese launch startup Orienspace secured funding for its reusable Gravity-2 rocket ahead of a targeted initial public offering. Defense sector updates saw the U.S. Space Force award $615 million across three firms to track airborne targets, the National Reconnaissance Office issue new synthetic aperture radar data contracts to three providers, and Australia agree to purchase American AIM-260 missiles. In scientific research, NASA’s IXPE space telescope provided observational evidence supporting a 90-year-old quantum theory involving ultra-magnetic stars, James Webb Space Telescope data indicated that a handful of galaxies drove early cosmic reionization, and South Korea’s lunar orbiter captured photos of a SpaceX rocket impact crater on the Moon. Looking ahead, space officials and researchers are watching preparations for Redwire’s upcoming Starfall microgravity research mission.
